newsitem.title: USA: New Hampshire approves utility bond issues.
newsitem.headline: New Hampshire approves utility bond issues.

text.p: The New Hampshire Business Finance Authority (BFA) has received approval of major financing packages for nearly $2 million in new business venture and construction projects, including three bond issues totaling more than $24 million for utility, high tech and solid waste incineration companies.

Gov. Stephen Merrill and the five-member Executive Council authorized the authority Wednesday to provide $8 million in Industrial Revenue Bonds for New England Power Company to refinance a portion of its debt.
BFA director Jack Donovan said the savings will be passed on to New Hampshire customers of the utility's subsidiary, Granite State Electric.

A $2.7 million bond issue to Elexsys International was also approved. The firm plans to acquire and renovate buildings for use in the manufacture of circuit boards and expects to create 100 new jobs and preserve 198 jobs, Donovan said.
The third approved bond issue provided $13.9 million in bonds to Wheelabrator Company of Claremont to refund outstanding bonds.

The refinancing is intended to reduce waste disposal costs for western New Hampshire and Vermont towns which are part of the New Hampshire/Vermont Solid Waste Project incinerator. Tipping fees are expected to be reduced as much as $20 for the communities because of the refinancing bond issue.

The BFA also received approval of 60 percent of a $2 million loan made by Citizens Bank to River Valley Fitness One Limited Partnership of Lebanon. The loan proceeds will be used to construct a 48,000 square foot halth club facility in Lebanon.
Other approved projects included two loan guarantee for two loans totalling $750,000 loan for the Jack Frost Company in Colebrook.
